summary: Phase 26 (harness and agent-contract remediation) is complete and gateable. All six tasks are done and carry their required orchestration/worker/reviewer evidence; each task has its own commit (26.1 393a427, 26.2 eda9361, 26.3 2b86665, 26.4 4b84925, 26.5 5bdf1a1, 26.6 a16059f). I independently verified the central claims rather than relying on the task reports: the amended phase-21 orchestration record's `subagents` array is the exact multiset concatenation of the fourteen 21.1-21.14 task records (56 entries) and its aggregate reconciles to every recomputed field; the change alters no phase-21 task report and only replaces the reduced aggregate plus appends a note. The contract rules and the 200->220 budget raise are present; docs/agent-contracts.md is exactly at 220 lines. Each of the C1-C7 corrections is present in its named prompt (eight files). I reproduced one sensitivity probe per new guard in an isolated copy (all-phases reviewer listing; from-phase-20 evidence completeness; from-phase-26 aggregate consistency) and confirmed each fails on a deliberately broken input and passes when restored, and reproduced the 26.5 collector's real fetch (exit 0, non-null total_tokens) and unreachable-server error (clear JSON, exit 1, no estimate, no credential leak even under bash -x). scripts/check-agents.sh and scripts/check-docs.sh both PASS on the current tree (check-docs self-skips the dotnet-generated-block section because dotnet is absent from PATH). The phase changed no product code, tests, artifact, or manifest: git diff 54e7aa9..HEAD touches only .opencode agents/scripts, docs, scripts/check-*.sh, and PLANS.md; artifacts/ArrTags_1.2.0.0.zip is byte-identical to its recorded identity, and there is no 1.3.0.0 artifact to touch. One MEDIUM finding remains: the new aggregate guard double-counts a phase-reviewer invocation recorded inside a task record, and phase 26 (26.6) is the first phase to have one, so the guard's recomputation inflates subagent_invocations_total and role_mix and double-counts 26.6's cost/tokens/duration; a semantically correct phase-26 aggregate FAILS the guard (reproduced). This should be fixed (or handled deliberately) before docs/implementation/phase-26/orchestration.json is written, but it does not affect the product phases or the artifact, so it does not block the phase. Two LOW documentation residuals are recorded. The tag v1.3.0-phase26 is the orchestrator's remaining step after this approval; I did not create it.

At the time of this review: tasks 26.1-26.6 are done and their acceptance criteria are met as written (26.3 meets 'both guards pass on the current tree' and 'a recorded sensitivity probe shows each new guard fails on a deliberately broken input and passes when restored' literally; its aggregate guard's role_mix/subagent_invocations_total edge is recorded as a MEDIUM finding below and does not change that literal determination); scripts/check-agents.sh PASS (15/15 ok) and scripts/check-docs.sh PASS (8 ok, generated-block section self-skipped because dotnet is absent) on the current tree; sensitivity probes are recorded in docs/implementation/26.3/worker-report.json for each new guard and independently reproduced; the phase review (this record) is the approval; the tag v1.3.0-phase26 is the one remaining orchestrator step and is expected only after this approval. findings.description: The new from-phase-26 aggregate guard double-counts a phase-reviewer invocation that is recorded inside a task record. Its role_mix, subagent_invocations_total and phase_reviewer_* / phase-total sums are computed as (all task-record invocations) + (every phase-reviewer entry in the phase record's own subagents array). Phase 26 is the first phase whose task records contain a phase-reviewer invocation: docs/implementation/26.6/orchestration.json records the advisory agent-process review as role phase-reviewer. Because the guard's own comment and the phase-20/21 precedent define the phase record's subagents as carrying the task-record invocations plus any phase-reviewer entries, that 26.6 entry lands in both the task-record set and the phase-reviewer set. The guard therefore recomputes subagent_invocations_total = 16 + 2 = 18 (the true distinct invocation count is 17), role_mix.phase-reviewer = 3 (true 2), and counts 26.6's cost/tokens/duration in both task_level_* and phase_reviewer_*, inflating the phase totals by 26.6's figures. This contradicts the guard's own comment at scripts/check-agents.sh:322-324 ('a phase-reviewer entry recorded inside a task record is already part of the task-level sums and is not counted twice'). I reproduced both directions in an isolated copy: a guard-shaped record written the natural way (task concatenation + gate phase-reviewer) passes; the semantically correct aggregate for the same invocation set (total 17, phase-reviewer 2, 26.6 counted once) FAILS with 'subagent_invocations_total: recorded 17 != recomputed 18' and 'role_mix: ... phase-reviewer:2 != ... phase-reviewer:3', plus double-counted cost/tokens/duration. The defect will be exercised for the first time when docs/implementation/phase-26/orchestration.json is written at this gate, so the permanent phase-26 aggregate is at risk of an overcount that the guard will not detect.

findings.recommended_action: Fix scripts/check-agents.sh so the phase-reviewer terms count only the phase record's OWN phase-reviewer entries (for example: compute role_mix and subagent_invocations_total directly over the phase record's subagents array, or exclude phase-reviewer entries whose session_id appears in a task record), and add a sensitivity-probe fixture whose conforming phase record includes a phase-reviewer entry contributed by a task record. Until the guard is fixed, when writing docs/implementation/phase-26/orchestration.json either (a) follow the guard's recomputation deliberately and record why the count differs from the distinct-invocation count, or (b) exclude 26.6's phase-reviewer entry from the phase record's subagents.

observations.observation: The recorded sensitivity probes for the new aggregate guard exercised a fabricated phase record whose subagents array contained only a synthetic phase-reviewer entry, not one contributed by a task record. Task 26.6, which is the first phase-26 task record to contain a phase-reviewer invocation, was produced after 26.3 was reviewed, so no probe covered the case that the phase-26 gate itself now creates; the guard's recomputation then double-counts it (see the MEDIUM finding).
evidence: docs/implementation/26.3/worker-report.json test_sensitivity (B2 conforming fixture uses 26.1/26.2 task records plus a synthetic phase-reviewer; no task-record phase-reviewer)
docs/implementation/26.3/orchestration.json notes ('the phase-26 aggregate branch is currently exercised only by a fabricated conforming record')
observations.proposed_change: Add a permanent sensitivity fixture for the aggregate guard whose conforming phase record includes a phase-reviewer entry contributed by a task record (e.g., a test task under docs/implementation/ that the check-agents.sh self-test drives), and fix scripts/check-agents.sh per the finding.
observations.rationale: A guard whose only probe omits the exact shape the next gate will produce cannot detect the double count; a fixture matching the real phase-26 shape would have failed first and prevented the defect from reaching the gate record.

observations.observation: The 26.4 attempt-2 invocation resumed the same session_id as attempt-1, so the orchestration record splits one session's cumulative usage into a snapshot entry (attempt 1) and a delta entry (attempt 2) that the phase aggregate then sums as if they were two independent invocations. The record's note documents the convention, but the shape is not derivable from the fields themselves and relies on manual arithmetic by the orchestrator.
evidence: docs/implementation/26.4/orchestration.json subagents[1] and subagents[2] (same session_id, attempt 1 snapshot + attempt 2 delta) and notes
.opencode/scripts/collect-session-usage.sh (emits a session's cumulative figures, not a per-invocation delta)
observations.proposed_change: Define the resumed-session recording convention in .opencode/agents/orchestrator.md's Subagent Execution Metadata section (an attempt that resumes a prior session records the delta and names the shared session_id), or add a --delta/since flag to .opencode/scripts/collect-session-usage.sh so the delta is machine-derived.
observations.rationale: The phase aggregate is a true sum only if snapshot+delta never overlap; a machine-derived delta removes the manual arithmetic that can silently double-count a resumed session.

observations.observation: Task 26.3's first worker attempt narrowed a pre-existing check: it replaced the ungated all-phases reviewer-report listing with the phase-20-scoped evidence check, and the test-quality reviewer caught it as TQ-01. The worker's own probe set did not include a regression check that the pre-existing guard still fired.
evidence: docs/implementation/26.3/worker-report.json acceptance criteria (B1 'replaces the weak reviewer-report state check')
observations.proposed_change: Add to the guard-task brief in .opencode/agents/orchestrator.md (or to .opencode/agents/implementation-worker.md) a requirement that a change touching an existing check include a regression probe demonstrating the pre-existing behaviour still fires.
observations.rationale: The correction worked, but only because a specialist review caught it; a cheap self-run probe would have found TQ-01 before review and saved one test-quality round.
